description.narrative: Capacity of health system to mitigate COVID-19 improved.

All eighteen project-supported COVID-19 facilities meeting WHO-endorsed quality standards for COVID-19 treatment (2020 Baseline: 0) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: a. 18 project facilities follow WHO - checklist. The checklist carefully aligns the hospital capacity requirements for COVID-19 with the capacity of each hospital: existing plans and capacities to manage epidemics and seasonal outbreaks of diseases such as influenza, and emphasizes the use of measures necessary to protect staff, other patients and visitors from infection; plans and capabilities for managing emergencies and disasters arising from other hazards; general and specialized services that are usually provided; assigned role during the COVID-19 pandemic, including any specific services it will offer.
Training institute engaged in April 2022. Data Source: MOH compliance checks based on WHO guidelines, midterm review special audit, and post-project special audit reports

Monthly infection incidence rate of health workers in project supported facilities retained at less than 1.5% (2020 baseline: 2%) Achievement: 1.4 Progress/Status: According to the Department of Disease Prevention and State Sanitary and Epidemiological Surveillance of the Ministry of Health of the Kyrgyz Republic, a total of 15 913 medical personnel in 18 project facilities were registered in Q4 2022. Of these, 7 were registered in 18 health care organizations, which is 0.00% of the total number of medical personnel. For the period Jan.-Dec 2022 were registered 232 infected medical personnel, which is 0.014% of the total number of medical personnel in 18 project facilities This figure increased due to the epidemic rise of COVID19 in June-July 2020. and June-July 2021. Data Source: MOH report, PIU assessment of facilities, midterm review special audit, and post-project special audit reports
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Capacity for infection prevention control and quality of care for COVID-19 patients improved. Indicator: Access to water and sanitation as needed, medical equipment and supplies, ambulances, proper sized PPEs, with suitable face masks and shields, and sanitary supplies (including menstrual kits) provided to all eighteen project-assisted facilities have access (2020 baseline: none) Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: Jan 2021 - initial contracts were negotiated by PIU directly with suppliers, however equipment selection and quantity still need to be verified, and MOH's request to expand facilities list needs to be approved through scope change. PIU civil engineer has visited all 8 sites to determine level of civil works required, cost estimates and bid documents are under development.
(Apr 2021- MOH requested additional facilities to be included in the project scope, which will require ADB approval. Minor change memo is being prepared. PIU civil engineer has visited all 8 sites to determine level of civil works required. Cost estimates were revised and bidding documents for civil works published.)
MOU midterm: PPEs have been procured under retroactive financing, but not yet fully delivered. Assessments of additional goods and access to water/sanitation at facilities conducted for original project facilities, pending for additional.
Apr 2022: PPEs have been procured under retroactive financing, and delivered to 71 MOH's facilities. Additional contract for medical supplies awarded in Apr 2022. Assessments of additional goods and access to water/sanitation at facilities conducted for initial facilities but not yet finalized.
July 2022: Contracts for the original goods packages have been awarded and delivery ongoing. Additional medical equipment using grant funds are being procured. RFQ for sanitary supplies is still to be advertised.
Q4 2022. Package for Sanitary Supplies was re-advertised after initial decision to cancel the package. Contract is awarded to Rospostavka LLC on 22 Dec 2022. Delivery is completed by 31 Dec 2022.
Data Source: MOH report, PIU project progress report

Output: Capacity for infection prevention control and quality of care for COVID-19 patients improved. Indicator: All medical staff 83% of whom are women) responsible for testing and treating COVID-19 patients in eighteen project-assisted facilities provided training on infection prevention control and patient management to treat COVID-19 cases and other infectious respiratory diseases (baseline: 0%) Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: Jan 2021 - training firm TOR being finalized by PIU/MOH and expected to be advertised by Q1 2021.
(Apr 2021 - training firm TOR being finalized by PIU/MOH and expected to be advertised by Q2 2021.)
MOU Midterm/Q3 2021 QPR: Protocols on infection prevention control and patient management have been developed, initial training has been delivered by MOH and WHO. Training firm supported by project to provide refresher trainings not yet recruited but TOR is already being finalized. Change in selection method memo is being prepared for SSS. Planned engagement Q1 2022.
Apr 2022: Training and assessment institute engaged in April 2022.
Q4 2022: Training and assessment institute submitted all reports per contract and had been paid by PIU. Data Source: Training firm report

Output: Capacity for infection prevention control and quality of care for COVID-19 patients improved. Indicator: All staff (83% female) at eighteen project-assisted facilities provided hardship allowances according to government regulation 194 (2020 baseline: none) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Jan 2021 - MHIF transfer instructions were approved in 2020. MOH has stated during Nov 2020 mission that hardship allowances for 2020 have already been paid through government budget. Calculations for allowances for 2021 are ongoing and may be disbursed this year if required.
(Apr 2021 - MHIF transfer instructions were approved in 2020. MOH has stated during Nov 2020 mission that hardship allowances for 2020 have already been paid through government budget, and no longer need project support. MOH has requested that MHIF funds be used in renovation of eight project-assisted facilities)
MOU Midterm/Q3 2021 QPR: According to the government regulation 194, hard work benefits have already been paid from the state budget for the project facilities. Project funds will be used for civil works only. Data Source: MHIF financial management report

Output: Capacity for infection prevention control and quality of care for COVID-19 patients improved. Indicator: Increase of 102 equipped beds with improved conditions including ICU and supply of 650 beds for treatment of patients with COVID-19 in project facilities (2020 baseline: none) Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: Jan 2021 - initial contracts were negotiated by PIU directly with suppliers, however equipment selection and quantity still need to be verified, and MOH's request to expand facilities list needs to be approved through scope change.
(Apr 2021- MOH requested additional facilities to be included in the project scope, which will require ADB approval. Minor change memo is being prepared. PIU civil engineer has visited all 8 sites to determine level of civil works required. Cost estimates were revised and bidding documents for civil works published.)
Apr 2022: Procurement of beds and other ICU equipment completed. Delivery is ongoing.
July 2022: Patient beds under the original contract delivered and installed. A new contract for additional beds was awarded in July 2022.
Q4 2022: 100% delivered under both original and additional contracts. Data Source: MOH report, PIU project progress report

Output: Capacity of surveillance and response services to COVID-19 strengthened. Indicator: All staff in project-supported COVID-19 facilities tested according to government-developed protocols (83% of whom are female) (2020 baseline: 0) Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: Jan 2021 - MOH has developed testing protocols for COVID-19 facilities. PIU M&E Specialist is currently collecting data at project facilities on testing capacity.
Ministry of Health of the Kyrgyz Republic approved order No. 649 on August 25, 2020 - Laboratory testing of each employee is performed before entering and after leaving the "red zone", i.e. every 14 days. Data collection from facilities ongoing for verification.
Q4 2022: All medical personnel (83% of them are women) working in the "red zone" are tested in accordance with the Interim Clinical Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Treatment of COVID-19 (version 4) approved by order of the Ministry of Health and Social Development of the Kyrgyz Republic of August 25, 2020 No. 649 Laboratory testing of each employee is performed before entering and after leaving the "red zone," i.e. every 14 days Data Source: MOH report, PIU assessment of facilities

Output: Capacity of surveillance and response services to COVID-19 strengthened. Indicator: At least 100,000 additional PCR tests conducted for COVID-19 (baseline April 2020: 26,000) Achievement: 1895073 Progress/Status: Jan 2021 - MOH has significantly scaled up testing capacity already, and is expected to surpass this target significantly even as supplies provided under ADB project have not yet been contracted.
(Apr 2021) Virology testing laboratories performed 114,000 molecular genetic analyses for SARS-CoV-2
Apr 2022: Virology testing laboratories performed 2 543 830 molecular genetic analyzes for SARS-CoV-2 as of March 31, 2022
Q4 2022: Virology testing laboratories performed 2 927 694 molecular genetic analyzes for SARS-CoV-2 as of September 30, 2022 Data Source: MOH report, PIU project progress report

Output: Capacity of surveillance and response services to COVID-19 strengthened. Indicator: COVID-19 diagnostic equipment, test kits, and reagents delivered to testing laboratories (baseline: not delivered) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: (Apr 2021 from annual report) Test kits and reagents procured by the government under retroactive financing. Additional need for supplies of testing consumables are under determination by the MOH and will be decided by Q2 2021.
Contract for supply was signed on 31 January 2022 with Altyn Tamyr CJSC. The Contract amount is USD 594 285,00. All goods were delivered and paid 100%.
MOU Midterm: On May 12, MOHSD sent a letter to the PIU to consider increasing the requirement for laboratory consumables to $670,000. PIU is working on approval of technical specifications with ADB specialists.
As of April 2022: Contract has been awarded.
As of June 2022: Delivery is ongoing for all items except for the ECG which will be sourced from China instead of Russia due to logistics constraints. Contract amendment was issued in July 2022 for the ECGs.
As of Oct 2022: Laryngoscopes with blades for newborns is expected to be delivered by October 20, 2022. Manual Ventilation Item (mask-valve-bag) for adults and ECG are expected to be delivered by November 15, 2022. Suction Units, 1L are expected to be delivered by November 20, 2022. All goods will be delivered and installed by November 30, 2022
Q4 2022: Delivery completed by 31 Dec 2022. 2,525,000 of PPE were purchased (FFP-3 respirators - 300,000 pcs. Overalls - 300,000 pcs. High shoe covers - 600,000 pcs. Gloves - 1 200 000 pcs. PPE set (medical gown, cap, surgical single-use MR masks, protective shoe covers) - 120,000 pcs. Protective goggles - 5,000 pcs) for a total amount of 3,132,700 USD. PPE distributed in 71 hospitals. Data Source: MOH report, PIU project progress report Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: 0 Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: 0 Target year: 2021 Target value: Y Actual value: Y
